page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-16 is a memory-oriented virtual machine configuration powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance provisions 16 dedicated vCPUs spanning 8 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading, backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 260 MB of shared L3 cache. It incorporates 124 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration includes Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for integer and tile matrix calculations, alongside full support for AVX-512 vector instruction sets. The server does not include bundled local storage or integrated graphics processing units, and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Empirical benchmark testing indicates distinct single-threaded computing advantages. The instance achieves top-decile results in Geekbench single-core performance with a score of 2250.0, accompanied by top-tier text processing metrics. Compression tests show strong execution, reaching 35.04 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 14.85 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Small-model language inference tests also register upper-quartile text generation throughput at 317.01 tokens/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics, including stress-ng multi-core CPU evaluations and PassMark database operations, sit firmly within the middle 50 percent of cloud instances. Memory bandwidth measures 111.3 GB/sec for uncached 256 MB reads and 50.44 GB/sec for writes.

Qualitatively, the server provides high resource density for scenarios that require significant memory footprints without scaling into higher core-count pricing tiers. The lack of bundled local NVMe storage represents an operational tradeoff, requiring external block storage for persistent state and input-output operations. The architecture is suited for in-memory databases, distributed memory caching such as Redis, enterprise data warehousing tasks, batch compression workloads, and CPU-bound artificial intelligence inference.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-16 is a memory-focused virtual machine instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 124 GB of system memory, providing an allocation of 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Driven by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz across 8 physical cores, the platform incorporates a 260 MB L3 cache alongside hardware support for AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance includes no local storage or attached GPUs, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates top-tier single-core Geekbench performance and strong single-threaded throughput in data compression tests, while multi-core compute and memory bandwidth results align with mid-range baselines. With its high memory-to-core ratio and instruction-level acceleration, the c4-highmem-16 configuration is well-structured for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, including in-memory databases, caching tiers, data analytics pipelines, and CPU-based machine learning inference tasks.
